parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence is documented; decriminalisation (2004), free LGBTI organisation registration, Pride since 2013, UN LGBTI core-group membership and a 2025 declaration naming transphobia show a protective state posture. No border, facility, custody or care restriction targeting trans visitors is sourced; these remain open questions, not exposures. The only trans-specific harm is one undated account of verbal abuse and two physical attacks against a resident activist — scattered, state-uninvolved, barely rate-moving. Negatives are mostly resident-facing (no legal gender recognition, no gender-identity workplace cover) or LGB-framed (80–82% neighbour-acceptance polls). No visitor-facing protection machinery is documented, so credit is withheld per rule 21. Net: low documented exposure, thin trans-specific data, working civil society.

entry_documents.exposure: No border or ID friction against trans visitors is sourced. The dossier notes no local precedent for documentary flexibility, so a marker/presentation mismatch is an open question, not a documented harm.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No acceptance of foreign X markers or chosen names is evidenced.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor carries a home passport; any mismatch handling at entry, hotels or police stops is unsourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrest, detention or custody practice targeting trans visitors appears in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No counsel, consular or advocate mechanism for trans visitors is evidenced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No custody-placement or strip-search rule is sourced, so a document-triggered investigation cannot be traced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility exclusion, ward-placement or birth-sex rule for visitors appears.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No facility access protection is evidenced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any hospital or shelter placement rule is unsourced; subnational texture is reputational only, with no enforcement comparison.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No care denial, medication seizure or ward misplacement for trans visitors is sourced. Gender identity is excluded from workplace discrimination grounds (resident-facing).
care_services.protection: Not documented. No health charter or visitor care guarantee appears.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care and HRT continuity rules for visitors are unsourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing documented. A 2010 foreign-government report found societal discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity continuing — dated, societal, not official.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documented: 2004 decriminalisation, UN LGBTI core-group membership, 2008 UNGA statement, 2025 regional declaration rejecting criminalisation and transphobic harassment.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective external posture is not shown to operate at border or police desks for visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No family-visiting, custody or conversion-practice risk to a travelling minor or guardian appears.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. The 2025 declaration calls for ending conversion practices — posture only.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian-minor dynamics, school or family exposure are unsourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One undated account (2016 interview) of verbal violence and two physical attacks against the country's first publicly out trans woman; 2010 report notes societal discrimination. No pattern, count or state involvement documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Free LGBTI organisation registration, Pride since 2013, country rated at tolerant end of its region (LGB-framed polls 80–82%).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence is unsourced; foreigner-status effect unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No visitor-facing recourse documented; the dossier explicitly lists border screening, facilities, custody, care and marker practice as unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning civil society (NGOs, Pride, UN engagement) and a 2024 UPR anti-discrimination commitment exist as climate signals.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions on entry, detention and care remain unresolved and cannot be scored as safe.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register bars and removes trans visitors with routine enforcement and no appeal. This dossier documents no entry bar, register, airline verification or exclusion mechanism — a materially lower-exposure regime. Similarity ends at bureaucratic uncertainty; the operative harm in 0.35-A is documented and continuous, whereas here it is absent.

Kestrel Isles has documented secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow, rarely-revised appeals. This dossier sources no screening or refusal practice at all, so exposure is lower; but it also documents no written decision, appeal desk or consular notification. Lower harm, thinner recourse — net slightly safer than 0.55-B.

Meridia documents trained border officers, an accepting document regime, a Civil Liberties Tribunal, counsel access and compensation for unlawful holding. This dossier has no documented border friction (favourable) but equally no documented training, tribunal or remedy (unfavourable). Absence of exposure offsets absence of protection; net sits just below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime shows no documented traveler-facing restriction: no criminalisation of trans identity, no entry bar, no facility or custody rule, no care denial, no state threat-framing. The state's posture is protective (decriminalisation 2004, UN core-group membership, 2025 declaration naming transphobia), and civil society operates freely. Against that, trans-specific acceptance is unmeasured (all polls are LGB-framed), no visitor-facing protection machinery is documented, and the sole trans harm — two undated physical attacks on a resident — is scattered and state-uninvolved. Border document flexibility, custody placement and care access are explicit open questions, not evidenced safety. The absence of documented visitor harms keeps the score above the 0.65 anchors; the absence of documented protections keeps it below 0.75.
